title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Has aprendido a diferenciar cuándo usar el Present Perfect (sin tiempo específico) y el Past Simple (con tiempo específico).

stages.title: Concepto Teórico: Present Perfect vs Past Simple

parts.visual: Usamos PAST SIMPLE para acciones que terminaron en un momento específico en el pasado. Se menciona el tiempo: yesterday, last week, in 2020. I finished the report yesterday (Terminé el reporte ayer).
parts.audio: We use Past Simple for actions that finished at a specific time in the past. We mention the time, like yesterday, last week, or in 2020. Example: I finished the report yesterday.

parts.visual: Usamos PRESENT PERFECT para experiencias o acciones pasadas sin decir CUÁNDO ocurrieron exactamente, importan en el presente. I have finished the report (He terminado el reporte - no digo cuándo).
parts.audio: We use Present Perfect for past experiences or actions without saying EXACTLY WHEN they happened. The result is important now. Example: I have finished the report.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el tiempo verbal correcto: Present Perfect o Past Simple.

questions.question: I ____ the client yesterday. (Visité - tiempo específico).
I ____ the new office. It looks great. (He visitado - sin tiempo).
questions.explanation: Sin tiempo específico (es una experiencia reciente): have visited.

questions.question: She ____ to Paris last month. (Viajó - tiempo específico).
questions.explanation: Con 'last month' usamos Past Simple: traveled.

questions.question: She ____ to Paris. She knows the city well. (Ha viajado - experiencia).
questions.explanation: Experiencia en su vida (sin fecha exacta): has traveled.

questions.question: We ____ the contract on Friday. (Firmamos).
questions.explanation: Con 'on Friday' usamos Past Simple: signed.

questions.question: We ____ the contract! Now we can start. (Hemos firmado).
questions.explanation: La noticia importante ahora (sin fecha exacta): have signed.

questions.question: ____ you see the email this morning? (¿Viste...?).
questions.explanation: Con 'this morning' (cuando la mañana ya pasó) es Past Simple: Did you see.

questions.question: ____ you seen the new catalog? (¿Has visto...?).
questions.explanation: Sin tiempo específico: Have you seen.

questions.question: He ____ the company in 2015. (Se unió a).
I ____ the manager about the issue. (He hablado con).
I ____ to the manager two hours ago. (Hablé con).
questions.explanation: Con 'ago' (hace) siempre usamos Past Simple: spoke.

questions.question: They ____ three new employees this week. (Han contratado - la semana no ha terminado).
questions.explanation: Con periodos de tiempo no terminados (this week, this year) usamos Present Perfect.

questions.question: They ____ three employees last week. (Contrataron).
____ you finish the report yesterday? (¿Terminaste...?).
I ____ this software many times. (He usado - experiencia).
questions.explanation: Experiencia repetida en el pasado hasta ahora = have used.

questions.question: I ____ this software for the first project. (Usé).
The meeting ____ at 9:00. (Empezó).
questions.explanation: Hora exacta en el pasado = Past simple.

questions.question: The meeting ____. (Ha empezado).
questions.explanation: Noticia reciente sin hora = has started.

questions.question: We ____ a lot of problems in 2020. (Tuvimos).
We ____ a lot of problems recently. (Hemos tenido).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe el verbo en Past Simple o Present Perfect (have/has + participio).

questions.question: I ____ the client yesterday. (visit - Past Simple)
I ____ ____ the new office. It looks great. (visit - Present Perfect)
She ____ to Paris last month. (travel - Past Simple)
She ____ ____ to Paris many times. (travel - Present Perfect)
We ____ the contract on Friday. (sign - Past Simple)
We ____ ____ the contract! (sign - Present Perfect)
He ____ the company in 2015. (join - Past Simple)
I ____ to the manager two hours ago. (speak - Past Simple)
I ____ ____ to the manager. (speak - Present Perfect)
____ you see the email this morning? (¿Viste? - Auxiliar)
